title: Listening for Core Meaning
focus: Captar intenção e ideia principal em enunciados curtos
verifiableTask: Identificar a mensagem central em seis falas

content.text: , mesmo sem entender todas as palavras.
Ao final da aula você consegue:
ouvir uma fala curta e dizer em uma frase:
“He wants to… / She is complaining about… / They are suggesting…”
identificar a mensagem central em seis falas.
os textos de listening estão em citações marcadas com 🎧. Leia em voz alta em ritmo natural; o aluno não deve olhar o texto antes de responder.
When you watch a series in English, do you understand everything? What do you do when you don't?
Is it easier to understand men or women? Fast or slow speakers? British or American accents?
What do you do when you don't understand a word in a conversation?
I usually get the general idea, but I miss details.
I get lost when people speak fast.
Could you say that again, please?
Verbos de intenção (o que a pessoa quer fazer)
They are complaining about the noise.
The professor reminds students about the test.
She warns him that the road is closed.
Pronúncia: fala conectada (como o inglês soa de verdade)
Ouça, compare e repita: primeiro devagar, depois rápido.
I can come tomorrow. · She can't find the room. · We can meet at noon. · He can't hear you. · You can borrow it. · They can't register yet.

questions.questionText: “I'm so sorry I missed the meeting.” The speaker is…
“Why don't we study at the library?” The speaker is…

explanations.B: Não está perguntando o motivo de verdade.

questions.questionText: “Don't forget the quiz is on Monday.” The speaker is…
She ______ to help me with the project. (ofereceu)

explanations.general: She offered to help me with the project.

questions.questionText: They are complaining ______ the noise.

explanations.general: They are complaining about the noise.

questions.questionText: In fast speech, “did you” often sounds like “didja”.

content.text: A ideia principal NÃO é a primeira palavra que você entende
Três perguntas para fazer enquanto ouve:
Qual é o problema ou o assunto?
a resposta errada muitas vezes repete palavras que você ouviu. A certa costuma usar
“Hey, I was wondering if you could send me your notes from Tuesday's lecture. I had a doctor's appointment and couldn't make it.”
Quem: um aluno para um colega.
Problema: faltou à aula de terça.
The speaker is asking for the lecture notes because he missed class.
Agora o aluno fala junto com o professor a frase do modelo (mesmo ritmo, mesma entonação).
→ suggesting a new time → complaining about the Wi-Fi → apologizing for the delay → offering a ride → reminding us about the deadline
I was wondering if you could
→ help me with the form → lend me your charger → explain the assignment → check my email
🎧 Professor lê cada fala uma vez. Aluno responde com
1. “Honestly, the printers in this lab never work. That's the third time this week.”
2. “If you want, I can drive you to the airport on Saturday.”
3. “Maybe we should start the presentation with the graph instead of the text.”
4. “Just a quick note: the lab report is due before midnight, not at the end of class.”
5. “Thanks, but I already have plans for Friday.”
Para cada fala acima, o aluno escolhe a frase que diz
a mesma coisa com outras palavras
a) The speaker turns down an invitation.
b) The speaker is unhappy with the equipment.
c) The speaker wants to confirm a detail.
d) The speaker proposes a change.
e) The speaker offers help with transportation.
f) The speaker reminds others of a time limit.

questions.questionText: “Honestly, the printers in this lab never work. That's the third time this week.” What is the speaker doing?

explanations.general: Correct answer: Complaining about the equipment

questions.questionText: “If you want, I can drive you to the airport on Saturday.” What is the speaker doing?
“Maybe we should start the presentation with the graph instead of the text.” What does the speaker want?

options.text: To change the order of the presentation

explanations.C: É o oposto: começar pelo gráfico.
explanations.general: Correct answer: To change the order of the presentation

questions.questionText: “The lab report is due before midnight, not at the end of class.” Main idea?

options.text: The deadline is earlier/different than students think.

explanations.general: Correct answer: The deadline is earlier/different than students think.

questions.questionText: “Thanks, but I already have plans for Friday.” What is the speaker doing?
“Sorry, did you say room 204 or 214?” What does the speaker want?

explanations.A: “Sorry” aqui não é desculpa de verdade.

questions.questionText: The correct answer often repeats the exact words you heard.

explanations.general: Falso: a resposta certa costuma ser uma paráfrase. Palavras repetidas são armadilha comum.

content.text: para dizer a mensagem central em uma frase e depois escolhe a alternativa.
“I tried to register for Biology 101 online, but the system says I need a permission code. Do you know who gives those?”
a) She wants to drop Biology 101. b) She needs information about getting a permission code. c) She is complaining about the professor.
“The cafeteria will stop serving breakfast at nine thirty starting next week, so plan accordingly.”
a) Breakfast hours are changing. b) The cafeteria is closing. c) Breakfast will be free next week.
“I really appreciate you staying late to help me with the experiment. I couldn't have done it alone.”
a) He is apologizing. b) He is thanking someone. c) He is inviting someone.
“Before you submit, double-check that your name is on every page. Last semester, a few reports got lost.”
a) The speaker is giving a warning/advice. b) The speaker lost a report. c) The speaker wants to read the reports.
“Do you think you could switch shifts with me on Thursday? I have an exam that morning.”
a) He wants to take an exam on Thursday. b) He asks to change work shifts. c) He is offering to work more.
“I don't think we need another meeting. We can solve this by email.”
a) She disagrees with having a meeting. b) She wants to schedule a meeting. c) She didn't receive the email.
o professor relê as falas e o aluno repete a fala 3 e a 5 (falar junto, mesmo ritmo).
[ ] Disse a intenção com um verbo correto (ask, suggest, complain…)?
Escreva uma fala sua para cada verbo de intenção (12 falas). Ex.:
suggest → “Why don't we take a break?”
. Depois grave 4 frases usando cada uma.
Assista a 3 minutos de uma série ou vídeo sobre universidade. Pause depois de 5 falas e escreva a intenção de cada.
Leia em voz alta as 6 falas da tarefa cronometrada, imitando a entonação natural. Grave a última leitura.
Tell me about a time you complained about something. What happened?
Reescreva as 6 falas da prática 4.2 com outras palavras.

questions.questionText: “You might want to bring an umbrella. It's supposed to rain later.” The speaker is…

explanations.A: Correto: “You might want to” = conselho educado.

questions.questionText: “Would you mind closing the window?” The speaker is…

explanations.general: Correct answer: making a polite request

questions.questionText: “I'm afraid I can't make it to your party.” The speaker is…
He ______ for being late. (pediu desculpas)
The teacher ______ us about the test on Monday. (lembrou)

explanations.general: The teacher reminded us about the test on Monday.

questions.questionText: “I wanna go” is the fast form of…

explanations.general: Correct answer: I want to go

questions.questionText: In “I can go”, the word “can” is usually weak and short.
